title: Work IQ: A2A and MCP tasks can ask for missing information or authorisation
summary: Hold: the spending-policy command incorrectly says PATCH and DELETE use the collection path; both require a policy ID. The roadmap details, billing model and monitoring path are supported, but Microsoft's conflicting descriptions of default write access should also be acknowledged.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-10-13T23:01:05.
Work IQ offers A2A, a remote MCP server and a REST API.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Work IQ A2A documents GetTask, CancelTask and SubscribeToTask for task management.
claims.quote: Work IQ supports the GetTask, CancelTask, and SubscribeToTask methods for managing tasks.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Work IQ A2A uses delegated Microsoft Entra ID authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ A2A uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP uses Microsoft Entra ID authentication.
claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP server uses Microsoft Entra ID for authentication.

claims.claim: Copilot Cowork documents MCP elicitation pausing execution to present a native form.
claims.quote: When an MCP server needs structured input from the user mid-tool-call—a confirmation, a picked option, a few form fields—it can use elicitation to pause execution and present a native form.

claims.claim: In that Cowork mechanism, tool execution resumes with the submitted data.
claims.quote: The user fills it out, submits, and tool execution resumes with the data.

claims.claim: Foundry's existing Work IQ MCP guidance says oauth_consent_request means the request awaits user authorisation.
claims.quote: An `oauth_consent_request` means the request is waiting for user authorization, not that retrieval succeeded.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the Work IQ elicitation feature itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation enable disable default authorization missing information paused task timeout resume billing pricing. Opened Work IQ overview, API overview, A2A overview, MCP overview and Cowork elicitation forms; no Work IQ elicitation description found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The elicitation default and whether existing A2A or MCP callers gain it automatically are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" admin policy Graph API enable default. Opened roadmap record, Work IQ A2A overview, MCP overview and policy governance; none states an elicitation default or automatic enablement for existing callers.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated who receives or may approve Work IQ elicitation requests.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" timeout task state resume authorization input recipients. Opened A2A overview, MCP overview, API overview and Foundry Work IQ consent passage; no elicitation recipient or approver specification found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The relationship between elicitation authorisation, new consent, action confirmation and existing consent is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation authorization agents consent admin controls prerequisites rollout answers storage. Opened Foundry Work IQ consent passage, A2A overview and MCP overview; existing OAuth consent is described, but its relationship to elicitation is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Permitted Work IQ elicitation input and whether it uses form mode or URL mode are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" timeout task state resume authorization input recipients. Opened Work IQ MCP overview, A2A overview and Cowork elicitation forms; only Cowork input modes are specified.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented where Work IQ elicitation answers go.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation authorization agents consent admin controls prerequisites rollout answers storage. Opened Work IQ overview, API overview, A2A overview and MCP overview; no elicitation-answer destination or storage description found.

claims.where: controls[3]; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: No elicitation-specific UI or API control to enable it or restrict requesting agents is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" admin policy Graph API enable default; Work IQ elicitation authorization agents consent admin controls prerequisites rollout answers storage. Opened MCP policy governance, A2A and MCP overviews; no elicitation switch or agent restriction found.

claims.claim: An automation endpoint for changing Work IQ MCP tenant policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy governance configure policy Microsoft Graph API PowerShell endpoint. Opened policy-governance-mcp and read search excerpts from the tool reference and migration guide; no policy-setting API or PowerShell call found.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The documented MCP policy control applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: The documentation qualifies access to the Policy tab as when it is available.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: The MCP policy page says mutation operations, including create, update, delete and actions such as sending email, are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.
claims.fix: Retain the attribution to the MCP policy page, but add that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq#work-iq-key-features says "Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply." Cite that page and advise checking the actual agent and tenant policy rather than treating the two descriptions as one universal default.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy evaluates each MCP tool request.
claims.quote: Policy layer | Applies tenant governance rules to each MCP tool request

claims.claim: Whether a resumed elicitation task is evaluated again is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" admin policy Graph API enable default; "Work IQ" "elicitation" timeout task state resume authorization input recipients. Opened MCP policy governance and A2A overview; no resumed-task evaluation semantics found.

claims.claim: Work IQ requests remain in the signed-in user's access context, and MCP policy cannot grant access beyond that user's permissions.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: The resumable lifetime of a paused Work IQ elicitation task is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" timeout task state resume authorization input recipients. Opened A2A overview and MCP overview; neither specifies an elicitation timeout or resumable lifetime.

claims.claim: The outcome when nobody answers a Work IQ elicitation request is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation" timeout task state resume authorization input recipients. Opened A2A overview, MCP overview and Cowork elicitation forms; Cowork cancellation behaviour is documented, but no Work IQ unanswered-request behaviour is specified.

claims.claim: The Cowork elicitation page says not all MCP hosts support elicitation.
claims.quote: Not all MCP hosts support elicitation yet.

claims.claim: Cowork guidance says never to request passwords, API keys or tokens through elicitation.
claims.quote: No secrets in forms. Never request passwords, API keys, or tokens via elicitation.

claims.claim: Add a spending policy in Microsoft 365 admin center through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: A limited monthly spending-policy budget caps monthly credits consumed within its scope.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: The spending-policy page says users who hit the limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.
claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.

claims.claim: GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE all operate on https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies.
claims.quote: Update spendingPolicy | PATCH `/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}` | Update a spending policy. ... Delete spendingPolicy | DELETE `/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}` | Delete a spending policy.
claims.fix: Replace the call in both front matter and rendered table with 'GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies (POST to create; PATCH and DELETE use https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id})'. The cited overview documents all four operations; PATCH and DELETE require the policy ID, as confirmed by its linked update and delete references.

claims.claim: The cost-management Graph APIs are beta and not supported for production applications.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/serviceUsageRecords?startDate=YYYY-MM-DD&endDate=YYYY-MM-DD lists service consumption for the selected day.
claims.quote: List costManagementServiceUsageRecords | GET `/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/serviceUsageRecords` | List reported consumption per governed service for one completed UTC day.

claims.claim: Service usage reports require startDate and endDate selecting one completed UTC day, with endDate exactly one day after startDate.
claims.quote: Completed UTC day | `startDate`, `endDate` | Date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Inclusive start and exclusive end. `endDate` must equal `startDate` plus one day, and its UTC midnight must not be later than the current time.
